okay, so the question is about tiling an 8x8 chessboard with 2x1 dominoes when two opposite corners are removed. let me think. dominoes cover two squares each, so the total number of squares must be even. an 8x8 board has 64 squares. if we remove two, we have 62 squares left, which is even. so that condition is satisfied.

but there's another thing to consider. the chessboard has alternating black and white squares. each domino covers one black and one white square. if we remove two opposite corners, what happens? the corners are both the same color. for example, the top-left and bottom-right corners are both black (assuming the top-left is black). removing two black squares means we have 32 - 2 = 30 black squares and 32 white squares. so now there's an imbalance: 30 black and 32 white. but each domino must cover one of each. so if there's a difference of two squares, it's impossible to pair them all up. hence, tiling isn't possible.

so the answer is no because of the color imbalance.
final_answer: it is not possible to tile the modified chessboard with 2x1 dominoes. each domino covers one black and one white square, but removing two opposite corners (which are the same color) creates an imbalance of 30 squares of one color and 32 of the other. since dominoes require equal numbers of both colors, the tiling cannot be completed.
